text:
Maria: quick question — I need to slice TTFT by customer tier and tokens/sec for a latency deep-dive. Looking for p50/p95/p99 plus a heatmap that separates batch vs realtime. Where should I start?

AJ: start with Grafana -> Observability / Latency Overview. There's a heatmap panel called "TTFT by route & concurrency". Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/ttft-overview (use the dropdowns to filter by model/customerTier). :mag:

Lee: if you want a direct PromQL to plug into the panel, try the token rate first: 

```
sum by(route, customer_tier)(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m]))
```

that gives tokens/sec per route+tier. then for latency quantiles (from our histograms):

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{kind="ttft"}[5m])) by (le, route, customer_tier))
```

Satoshi: small tips —
- use kind="ttft" label to avoid conflating streaming vs completion latency
- use [5m] windows for p95, [1m] for p50 if you need tighter recency
- drop customer_tier="internal" if you're only looking at external customers

Maria: thanks. Any recommended panel to compare p50/p95/p99 side-by-side with tokens/sec? I want correlation (are spikes at 3k tokens/sec causing p95 jumps).

AJ: yes — the "Route correlation view" has stacked panels: tokens/sec (line), p50/p95/p99 (lines), and a heatmap of request latency buckets. If you don't have permissions to edit, clone the dashboard and add a template variable for model.

Lee: If you want to create an ad-hoc heatmap (latency buckets vs token rate) you can do a two-axis panel: heatmap from request_latency_seconds_bucket (count per bucket) and tokens/sec as an overlaid line. It's noisy but shows correlation.

Maria: what about alert tuning? folks suggested p95 500ms for realtime routes but it flaps. Any ideas for thresholds that reduce noise?

Satoshi: two approaches we use:
1) use rate-limited alerts: require p95 > 500ms for 5m + error-rate < threshold (to avoid noisy alerts during infra blips)
2) use dynamic baseline (seasonal) alerts: alert if p95 > baseline*1.5 where baseline is 30d median.

AJ: example alert rule (Prometheus style):

```yaml
- alert: HighTTFTP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{kind="ttft"}[5m])) by (le, route, customer_tier)) > 0.5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "p95 TTFT > 500ms for route={{ $labels.route }} tier={{ $labels.customer_tier }}"
```

AJ: tweak `for:` to 10m makes it much less chatty. Also scope alerts to customer_tier=production usually.

obs-bot: Alert HighTTFTP95 fired for route=generate-text, customer_tier=enterprise at 1767005280

Maria: ack — thanks. For tracing, where do I pull full traces when I see a p95 spike?

Lee: traces -> Jaeger link on the dashboard. You can click a heatmap cell to open a sample trace. Or use curl to fetch spans from our trace API: 

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBS_API_TOKEN" "https://tracing.redwood.internal/api/traces?service=inference&tag=route:generate-text&start=1767004800&end=1767005400"
```

Satoshi: also check KV cache hit rate panel — cache misses often push us into the slow path and bloat TTFT. There's a cache_hit_ratio per model route variable.

Maria: perfect. I'll pull the p95 timeseries for the past 2 hours scoped to enterprise and attach findings to the ticket. Thanks all :pray:

AJ: ping if you want me to add a temp dashboard with the exact slices.

Lee: added a bookmark in our docs: https://wiki.redwood.company/obs/ttft-heatmap-guide

Maria: wonderful, closing the loop.
